# AGENTS.md

<!-- agent-flow:start v0.2.0 -->
<!-- Reusable workflow block. Same in every repo. Do not edit per project. -->

## 1. How we work

There are two ways to work. Pick one at the start.

- **Feature → slice.** New behavior, API or contract change, data model change, auth/permissions/payments, frontend + backend together, or a design decision. Use the slice workflow below.
- **Small change → normal chat.** Clear bug fix, text/style tweak, small refactor in one area, config or test fix. Work on a branch, run the checks, and merge following the project's git policy (section 10). No slice.

If unsure, ask the human. If a small change grows into a feature, stop and suggest a slice.

## 2. Slices and phases

A slice is one feature in `slices/NNNN-<name>/`, on its own branch and worktree (section 10). Read and edit its files in that worktree, not in the main checkout.

```
brainstorm → spec → plan → ready → implementing → integration → preview → done
                                     any phase → blocked | cancelled
```

When each phase starts: `workflow/formats/lifecycle.md`.

```
slices/NNNN-<name>/
  spec.md        what the feature does        human approves
  plan.md        how it will be built         human approves
  notes.md       technical ideas from the spec interview, optional, not approved
  status.md      overview, generated by flow  never edit
  tasks/         one file per task
  reviews/       review reports
  history/       approved snapshots
  events.jsonl   state and history
```

Templates: `workflow/templates/`.

Ideas parked for later go to `backlog.md` at the project root when a slice is done.

Contracts, the data model, and other living docs stay at the project level (see section 9). A slice edits them on its own branch and lists them under `touches` in `plan.md`. The human approves the slice's change to them, not the whole file.

### Tracks

The lead proposes a track in `plan.md`. The human approves it with the plan.

- **complex:** the slice changes a contract or the data model, touches more than one part (e.g. backend and frontend), or involves security.
- **simple:** everything else.

| | simple | complex |
|---|---|---|
| Spec check | short: up to 5 questions, before the human approves the spec | same |
| Plan review | light: checks 1-4 in `workflow/roles/plan-reviewer.md` | full |
| Task review | core tasks only | every task |
| Integration review | always | always |

## 3. Roles

| Role | Does | Instructions |
|---|---|---|
| Human | decides, approves, previews | — |
| Lead | the main chat agent: designs with the human, writes docs, runs the slice, reports | `workflow/roles/lead.md` |
| Worker | implements exactly one task | `workflow/roles/worker.md` |
| Plan reviewer | asks questions about the spec before approval; checks spec, plan, contract, tasks together before coding | `workflow/roles/plan-reviewer.md` |
| Code reviewer | checks one task, or the whole slice | `workflow/roles/code-reviewer.md` |

If you are the main chat agent, you are the lead. Read your role file before starting slice work.

## 4. Hard rules

- Only a human approves. Never approve for them, even if asked to "just continue".
- Never change an approved spec, plan, or contract. If it looks wrong, stop and ask.
- Never edit `events.jsonl`, `status.md`, anything in `history/`, or a submitted review.
- Change status only with `flow` commands.
- Merge or push only as the project's git policy allows (section 10), and for a slice only after the human approves the result.
- Never force-push. Never rewrite shared history.

## 5. Stop rules

Stop, mark the task `blocked`, and tell the human in plain words when:

- a task fails its checks 3 times since its last review
- a review (plan, task, or integration) still does not pass after 3 rounds
- the task is unclear, or the spec, plan, or contract looks wrong
- you need a new dependency, a storage format change, secrets, or CI changes

## 6. Status

- **Read:** the slice's `status.md`, or `flow status`, `flow findings`, `flow brief`.
- **Write:** `flow` commands only.
- **Lifecycles** of slice phases, documents, tasks, findings, and checks: `workflow/formats/lifecycle.md`. Read it before changing any status.
- **Checks:** a task moves to review or done only after `flow check` passes. Only `flow check` counts, not tests you run yourself.

`status.md` is the overview of the whole slice: what needs the human, documents, tasks, findings from all reviews, and the log. `flow` rebuilds it from `events.jsonl`, the task files, and the submitted reviews. Format: `workflow/formats/status.md`.

> **Bootstrap mode:** `flow` does not exist yet. Until it does, the lead does by hand what `flow` would write: `status.md` (in the same format, with a dated Log line for every change), the managed header fields of spec, plan, task, and review files (including `verdict` and `submitted_at`), and new files in `history/`. Everyone else reads them. `events.jsonl` is not written in bootstrap mode; `flow` will build it later from `status.md` and git history.

## 7. Skills

| Skill | Use when |
|---|---|
| `flow-setup` | checking whether a repo is ready for the workflow, and setting up what is missing: workflow files, checks, test dependencies, hooks, CI |
| `flow-spec` | brainstorming a feature and writing its spec |
| `flow-plan` | writing plan, contract, and tasks, and getting them reviewed |
| `flow-implement` | running the tasks with workers and reviewers |
| `flow-review` | starting a review (spec, plan, task, or whole slice) in a fresh context, and acting on its verdict |

## 8. Project

agent-flow is a spec-driven workflow for AI coding agents. It has three parts: the workflow files (this file, skills, roles, templates), a `flow` CLI that records workflow state, and a read-only web dashboard.

We build agent-flow using its own workflow.

## 9. Stack profile

| Part | Folder | Tech |
|---|---|---|
| CLI + shared packages | `cmd/flow/`, `internal/` | Go |
| Dashboard backend | `cmd/dashboard/` | Go, reuses `internal/` |
| Dashboard frontend | `web/` | React + Vite + TypeScript |
| File formats | `schemas/` | JSON Schema |
| Workflow files | `workflow/`, `.agents/skills/` | Markdown |

Connections:

| From → To | Contract |
|---|---|
| Dashboard frontend → dashboard backend | `contract/dashboard-api.yaml` (OpenAPI) |

Tools per role (the lead is the tool you chat in):

| Role | Tool |
|---|---|
| Worker | Codex |
| Code reviewer | Claude Code |
| Plan reviewer | Claude Code |

Always allowed in any task (no need to list in `touches`):

- Generated code: `internal/api/gen/`, `web/src/api/gen/`
- Lock files: `go.sum`, `web/package-lock.json`, only when `go.mod` / `package.json` did not change

Auto-fix, run by `flow check` before the checks, for the parts a change touches. They change only layout, or apply fixes the tool marks as safe:

| Part | Folder | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Go | `.` | `gofmt -w cmd internal` |
| Web | `web/` | `npx eslint --fix .` |

Checks, for the parts a change touches:

| Part | Tier | Folder | Command | Passes when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Go | task | `.` | `gofmt -l cmd internal` | it prints nothing |
| Go | task | `.` | `go vet ./...` | exit code 0 |
| Go | task | `.` | `go test ./...` | exit code 0 |
| Web | task | `web/` | `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit code 0 |
| Web | task | `web/` | `npx eslint .` | exit code 0 |
| Web | task | `web/` | `npx vitest run` | exit code 0 |
| Web | task | `web/` | `npx vite build` | exit code 0 |

Tiers: `task` runs on every `flow check`. `slice` runs once all tasks are done, before the integration review.

Test dependencies (checks start these themselves; never shared services):

| Dependency | Used by | In checks | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Git repositories | CLI, dashboard | yes | temporary repos created by the tests |
| GitHub API | dashboard (later) | fake | fake server in the tests |

Known gaps (chosen in setup; revisit when possible):

- Workflow files (Markdown) have no automatic checks. Reviewers check them by hand. Chosen by bert-pratya, 2026-10-17.
- No pre-commit hook and no CI job yet: errors are found only by the checks a worker runs. Slice 0001's setup task adds them. Chosen by bert-pratya, 2026-10-17.

## 10. Project rules

### Git policy

- Base branch: `main`
- Slice branch: `slice/NNNN-<name>` from `main` (or from another slice's branch when stacked, `--after`), worktree `.flow/worktrees/NNNN-<name>/`
- Task branch: `task/NNNN-NN` from the slice branch, worktree `.flow/worktrees/task-NNNN-NN/`
- Small changes: `fix/<short-name>` from `main`
- After the human approves the result: the agent merges into `main` and pushes to `origin`
- Remotes: `origin` is private and gets the full history. `public` gets only releases: never push to it. At a release, the human asks, and the project is pushed there as one squashed commit. A local pre-push hook refuses anything else.
- Slices update from `main` before the integration review, and again just before merging. A conflict becomes a fix task.
- Parallel slices: merge one at a time.
- Commits: one per task, plus one per fix round, message `NNNN/NN: <what changed>`

### Other rules

- Until the first release of `flow`, this repo always runs in bootstrap mode, even when a `flow` binary exists. Never use `flow` to manage this repo's slices. Use it only in tests, on temporary repos.
- Write in plain, simple English. Short sentences.
- Keep everything generic. No company names, internal URLs, or secrets in this repo.
- Shared Go logic goes in `internal/`, not `cmd/`. The CLI and the dashboard must use the same packages to read and validate files.
- Every change that adds behavior adds a test for it.
- `flow` makes no network calls. It reads and writes repo files and runs git and the check commands. (The dashboard's GitHub access, later, is the one exception, and it is off by default.)
- `flow` works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Test path, line-ending, and process handling on all three. Run each check as a separate command, not as a shell string.
